name: Michal
bio:
Michal was Saul's younger daughter, who later became David's wife and risked her own safety to help him escape her father's attempt to kill him — a marriage that began in love and ended, as the rest of 1 and 2 Samuel will show, in painful estrangement.

Scripture first names her while listing Saul's household, alongside her older sister Merab (1 Samuel 14:49). After David's fame grew following Goliath's defeat, Saul learned that Michal loved David and was pleased, scheming to use the marriage to get rid of him; he demanded a bride price of a hundred Philistine foreskins, hoping David would die obtaining them. David instead killed two hundred Philistines and delivered the full number, and Saul had no choice but to give him Michal in marriage (1 Samuel 18:20-27).

Later, when Saul again sent men to watch David's house and kill him at dawn, Michal learned of the plot and lowered her husband through a window so he could flee under cover of night; she then placed a household idol in the bed, covering it with a garment and goat hair to deceive the men sent to seize him, buying David precious time to escape. When Saul confronted her afterward for letting his enemy go, Michal falsely claimed David had threatened to kill her unless she helped him (1 Samuel 19:11-17). Michal's quick-witted, decisive rescue allowed David to escape and begin his years as a fugitive.

During David's years as a fugitive, Saul gave Michal in marriage to Palti son of Laish of Gallim instead (1 Samuel 25:44) — a marriage that would later be forcibly undone after David became king, casting a shadow over his relationship with Michal from then on, a story told in detail in 2 Samuel.
